title: Build a chat client with the Foundry SDK
learningObjective: Create a lightweight chat client application with the Foundry SDK (azure-ai-projects) and the Responses API.

prerequisites.text: Deploy a model in the portal

foundation: The Foundry SDK for Python (azure-ai-projects) connects your code to your Foundry project. It gives you an OpenAI-compatible client to call your deployed models.
You need three things: the project endpoint, a credential (your Azure sign-in), and the deployment name.
A chat client sends the conversation so far plus the new message, and prints the reply. Keeping the history is what makes it a conversation.
engineer: Install: pip install "azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0" azure-identity. Create AIProjectClient(endpoint=FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT, credential=DefaultAzureCredential()). The endpoint looks like https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>.
DefaultAzureCredential uses az login locally and managed identity in Azure, so no keys are stored in code. The identity needs a role such as Azure AI User on the project or resource.

openai = project.get_openai_client(); response = openai.responses.create(model='<deployment>', instructions='<system prompt>', input=<text or message list>); print(response.output_text). response.usage shows input and output tokens.

Conversation state: append each user and assistant message to a list and send it as input, or use the conversations API to store history server-side. Trim or summarise history to stay within the context window.

azure-ai-projects 2.x isn't compatible with 1.x code; older samples using azure-ai-inference or AzureOpenAI clients are superseded by this approach. Handle errors: 401/403 (credential or role), 404 (deployment name), 429 (rate limit, retry with backoff).

animation.caption: Configure endpoint, credential and deployment name, then diagnose common SDK errors.

example.title: A terminal chat helper
body: A developer builds a 30-line Python chat client for the returns assistant: AIProjectClient with DefaultAzureCredential, a history list, and responses.create with the system prompt as instructions.
It failed first with 404 because the code used the model family name instead of the deployment name 'chat-model'.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with access to Microsoft Foundry (ai.azure.com)
permissions: Azure AI User on the Foundry project to use models and agents; Azure AI Project Manager or Owner to create projects and deployments
limits: Model availability differs by region and deployment type
Deployments have tokens-per-minute (TPM) rate limits and quota per subscription and region
portal: Project Overview: copy the project endpoint.
Access control (IAM) on the Foundry resource: assign Azure AI User to your account or app identity.
Set FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT, run az login, run the script.
configuration.cli:
# Create a Foundry resource and project (billable only when used)
az group create --name rg-ai901 --location eastus2
az cognitiveservices account create --name contoso-ai --resource-group rg-ai901 \
  --kind AIServices --sku S0 --location eastus2 --custom-domain contoso-ai --allow-project-management
az cognitiveservices account project create --name support --resource-group rg-ai901 --account-name contoso-ai
# Deploy a model (Global Standard, 50K TPM)
az cognitiveservices account deployment create --name contoso-ai --resource-group rg-ai901 \
  --deployment-name chat-model --model-name gpt-5-mini --model-version <version> --model-format OpenAI \
  --sku-name GlobalStandard --sku-capacity 50
# Give your user access to the project
az role assignment create --assignee <user-or-identity> --role "Azure AI User" \
  --scope $(az cognitiveservices account show -n contoso-ai -g rg-ai901 --query id -o tsv)
configuration.powershell:
New-AzResourceGroup -Name rg-ai901 -Location eastus2
New-AzCognitiveServicesAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-ai901 -Name contoso-ai -Type AIServices -SkuName S0 -Location eastus2 -CustomSubdomainName contoso-ai
# Projects and deployments: use the Foundry portal or Azure CLI
New-AzRoleAssignment -SignInName user@contoso.com -RoleDefinitionName 'Azure AI User' -Scope (Get-AzCognitiveServicesAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-ai901 -Name contoso-ai).Id
configuration.python:
# pip install "azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0" azure-identity
import os
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient

project = AIProjectClient(
    endpoint=os.environ["FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT"],  # https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>
    credential=DefaultAzureCredential(),
)
openai = project.get_openai_client()

history = []
while True:
    text = input("You: ")
    if not text:
        break
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
    response = openai.responses.create(
        model="chat-model",  # your deployment name
        instructions="You are Contoso's returns assistant. Answer in at most three sentences.",
        input=history,
    )
    print("Assistant:", response.output_text)
    history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response.output_text})

troubleshooting.symptom: DefaultAzureCredential failed to retrieve a token.
troubleshooting.cause: Not signed in and no managed identity.
troubleshooting.fix: Run az login or configure a managed identity.
Append messages to the input list or use conversations.

comparisons.difference: Responses is the newer API used by Foundry samples, with built-in tools and conversations; Chat Completions is the older message-list API.
Entra ID avoids storing secrets and supports RBAC.

misconceptions.myth: You need the model's API key in code.

misconceptions.reality: Each call is stateless unless you send history or use conversations.

architectureDecisions: Keep the endpoint and deployment name in configuration.
